verdict.rationale: Pigment's security docs describe fine-grained data access rights that determine who can see and modify specific data within applications. That covers the core need: a budget owner can view and edit their own numbers while other data stays restricted. The knowledge base also lists permissions as a collaboration feature. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of scoping by department or dimension member (e.g., restricting by cost center), in-depth configuration docs for read vs. write rights, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, department-scoped permissions let a budget owner see and edit their numbers without exposing the whole company

citations.quote: fine-grained data access rights for all data within your Pigment applications, allowing you to determine who can see and modify specific data
collaborate effectively in Pigment with shared views, comments, permissions, and notifications
